findings.message: A finding with a missing or unknown class is handled inconsistently. In the fast-track round, an `unclassified` blocker stays blocking (fail closed). The same finding written to debt.md or follow-ups.md is stored as `class:other`, and `specclaw-sync release` never blocks on `other`. So the release gate, which reads those lists, fails open on the exact input the round gate fails closed on. Fix: write a distinct marker for unclassified items (for example `class:unclassified`), and have `specclaw-sync release` treat that marker, or a missing marker on a review-written item, as blocking.
findings.scenario: Fast track is on and the default block_on applies. The model returns a pre-existing blocker (`in_delta:false`, `scenario` set, no `class`), such as "SQL injection in a.py". It is excluded from `block` as pre_existing, so `append_debt` writes `- [ ] [other blocker ...] <!-- fp:... class:other -->`. Then `specclaw-sync release base HEAD` lists it as `other` and exits 0. The same finding labelled `class:security` exits 1.

findings.message: Several rules exist twice and can drift apart: `CLASSES`, `DEFAULT_BLOCK_ON`, the class normaliser (`norm` vs `_class_token`) and the `release_gate.block_on` parser (a hand-rolled regex here, `parse_block` in review_core.py). The parity test only covers 12 fixed configs. A form outside that table, such as a multi-line flow list `block_on: [law,\n  security]`, is parsed by each copy independently. Consider importing one shared definition, or at least asserting that the two `CLASSES` tuples are equal in the parity test.

`class GateError` sits between the module constants, and `LIST_RE`/`CLASS_RE` follow it with no blank lines, so the constants are split around the class. Move the class below all the constants (PEP 8: two blank lines around top-level definitions).

This step runs under `set -euo pipefail`. When the iterations GET fails, or returns an empty `value`, the `ITER=$(curl ... | python3 ...)` assignment aborts the step with a generic non-zero exit, and the planned warning ('latest iteration is not ...; status not posted') is never printed. The GitHub template and the CLI helpers instead surface this as 'not posted'. Guard the read with `|| ITER=""` and emit an explicit warning that the iteration could not be read.
